_comment: REGION OWNERSHIP -- the input to the ST3 interlock (tracker/reimpl.yaml).
A SEPARATE FILE, and that is not tidiness. tools/data/state_regions.json is REBUILT by
`gen_state_registry.py --refresh` out of the five address manifests, so a hand-added field there
would be silently dropped the next time anyone refreshed. Ownership is a HUMAN DECLARATION about
a region -- nothing measures it -- so it lives in its own committed file and is merged in.
TWO PROPERTIES, AND CONFLATING THEM IS THE WHOLE TRAP:
l1_serializer  -- a module answers 'what is this region's content?' with a canonical stream
instead of the consumer reading bytes at an address. mh::orders has done
this for QUEUE and QUEUE_COUNT since ST4.
owned_by_dll   -- the region has PHYSICALLY LEFT the binary: its bytes are somewhere the DLL
allocated, and the .bss address it used to occupy is abandoned memory.
Claiming is not moving (see state/region_owner.h). While Law 1 freezes a layout an original
accessor still reads, an owner's own pointer IS the frozen .bss address -- so a region can be
fully L1-served and still be at its stock address, which is exactly the state orders is in today.
THE RULE the interlock enforces, checked by gen_state_registry.py --check:
1. A region with owned_by_dll and NO l1_serializer that ANY manifest still reaches by address
is an ERROR, naming the region and the manifest. Its bytes are not where that address is.
2. A region with owned_by_dll AND a serializer is still an ERROR for any manifest whose window
is not the WHOLE region -- a sub-window or a SHIFTED block cannot be served by the module
(mh::state::owner_serves requires offset==0 and len==size), so it would fall back to the raw
address, which is precisely the abandoned memory.
NOTHING IS owned_by_dll TODAY. The rule ships INERT AND ARMED -- the same shape as C1's patch/seam
interlock -- and the evidence that it works is the negative test (`--selftest`), not a green run.
The first real entry will be an AI island region under AI1-P; the measurement that makes that safe
is already recorded in ST3's tracker entry (none of the AI's 28 island regions appears in any save
block, so the island move does not touch the save format at all).
Every one of the 554 registry regions also carries `owner_subsystem` + `why`. This is a THIRD
independent property, and conflating it with the two above is the same trap as conflating those
two with each other:
owner_subsystem -- WHOSE state this is: the subsystem that owns its content and lifecycle. It
says nothing about where the bytes live or who serves them.
WHY IT EXISTS. 'Own all the writers of sim state' is not a finite claim until each region has one
owner. Measured against the 152 regions the migrated sim writes, the 169 external writers included
32 presentation/render and 7 input/selection functions -- and what they write is almost entirely
UI-owned flags (STRAT_UI_BLDG_PANEL_REFRESH_PENDING has 11 external writers, 10 of them UI; the
chat-input line; the cam-pan targets; the selected-building index). Those want RE-ATTRIBUTION, not
migration. Without an owner per region, 'own all writers' reads as a mandate to migrate the
renderer.
VOCABULARY: _subsys.OWNER_SUBSYSTEMS -- the shared subsystem taxonomy minus 'Other named' (that
bucket is for FUNCTIONS whose symbol is off-convention, i.e. a naming gap, and a naming gap cannot
own state), plus the sentinel `unattributed`. The sentinel is narrow by construction: rule 8
accepts it only for a region the state matrix never saw touched at all (8 today, all
measured:false auto-labelled literals).
CROSS-WRITES. After the owner is declared, an original writer of a DIFFERENT subsystem is a
cross-write, and it must be answered rather than left standing: either the owner is wrong
(re-attribute it) or the cross-write is a fact about the code, recorded in
`cross_write_accepted`. gen_region_accessors.py --check FAILS on an unadjudicated one, and
--worklist prints them. The reason string starts with a CLASS TAG so the residue is countable:
init-only         session/boot initializers and resetters write everything at session start;
that is not an ownership claim
config-load       a cfg/map loader populates a static table from disk
naming-gap        the cross-writer is [Other named] -- its subsystem is unknown, not different
misfiled-writer   the writer's NAME misfiles it (llm_strat_ui_*, game_SetEvent, the
llm_strat_group_* AI family)
shared-mode-flag  a genuinely cross-cutting global (game mode, window size, cursor)
producer-consumer another subsystem legitimately hands a value across a seam
debug-tool        llm_debug_console_dispatch can poke arbitrary globals from the dev console
shared-record     two subsystems own disjoint FIELD GROUPS of one record (player_data); a
layout split is a Law-1 change and out of the current ledger (SB3 D1)
pending-migration the writer really does belong to the owner's subsystem and is simply not
renamed/migrated yet -- a REAL worklist row, not an excuse
THE BOUNDARY, stated rather than discovered later: the registry is not every global in the
binary. 2057 of the state matrix's 2596 referenced regions resolve into no registry region at all.
This file adjudicates the registry; it does not claim to have adjudicated the address space.
WRITERS ONLY. Readers are cross-cutting by nature (471 external accessors, most of them reads); a
rule demanding a reason for every cross-subsystem READ is one nobody would satisfy honestly. The
boundary decision (SB3 D3) is stated in terms of writers for the same reason.
`serializer_why` is the OLD `why` from before SB2: it explains the l1_serializer claim, which is a
different sentence from why a subsystem owns the region. `why` is now the owner's reason.
HAND-MAINTAINED. The 554 seed declarations were produced once by
tools/oneoff/2026-08-23-seed-region-owners.py (a 16-agent read-only adjudication of the 227
regions whose name and measured writers disagreed, + a name-taxonomy default for the rest, +
central review); after that this file is edited by hand. gen_state_registry.py --check refuses an
unclassified region and its message carries the taxonomy's SUGGESTION, so a newly merged region is
a one-line edit -- but a suggestion is not a declaration and nothing writes it for you.
---- D4 / SB-SOLE (2026-09-10): WHAT `owned_by_dll` MEANS NOW, AND WHAT `relocated` IS -------
The block above is the ORIGINAL, ST3-era definition and it is kept because it is still the
definition of the STRONGER claim -- which simply is not called `owned_by_dll` any more.
owned_by_dll -- LIBMH BINDS THIS REGION, and no original function writes it. This is D4's
redefinition (docs/state-boundary.md D4: `the bytes have physically left the
binary` -> `libmh binds this region`) landed in the data and in the rule
text. Its release condition is the ONE surviving clause of D3: the external
WRITER count is zero. Nothing moves.
relocated    -- the old sentence, now under its own name: the bytes are somewhere the DLL
allocated and the .bss address is abandoned memory. It is a LADDER on top of
owned_by_dll, not an alternative to it (rule 9 refuses relocated without
owned_by_dll), and it is what arms rules 1-3 and rule 6.
WHY THE SPLIT HAD TO HAPPEN HERE. SB-BIND's done_when asked for the redefinition and it never
landed -- the _comment above and every rule in gen_state_registry still carried `physically
left the binary`. Measured 2026-09-10: marking the 310 qualifying regions under the redefined
meaning produced 666 interlock violations, and ALL 666 were rules 1, 3 and 6 -- exactly the
three D4 retired for the hosted configuration. Rules 4 (an original writer remains) and 5
(unmeasured) fired ZERO times, which is the same statement as `SB-SOLE's boundary holds`. So
the rules were not wrong, they were keyed to the wrong claim.
EXTERNAL READERS ARE NOT REQUIRED TO BE ZERO, and this paragraph exists so a later session does
not re-derive the rejected option. In the hosted configuration the host answers the bind table
with the stock .bss base, so an original reader of an owned region reads THE LIVE BYTES LIBMH
JUST WROTE -- there is nothing stale to read. The reader clause was never protecting
correctness in place; it was protecting against a region that had MOVED out from under its
readers, which is why it now keys on `relocated` and is the standalone build's gate (LIB-REF)
rather than dead code. Owning the readers as well was measured and rejected on its own numbers:
305 functions / 117 KB, docs/state-boundary.md option (a). Writers are different in kind, not
in degree -- an original WRITER means two implementations of one piece of state, which is a
live desync/corruption hazard in the hosted build too.
kept_writers / kept_writers_why -- the OTHER legal outcome of SB-SOLE, per region. A region
libmh writes either reaches zero external writers (mark it owned_by_dll) or
keeps them for a named reason, and then it lists them HERE, exactly, so a
standing reason cannot silently absorb a new writer. Rule 10 refuses a
missing record, a list that disagrees with the census, a stale one, one
alongside owned_by_dll, and an empty `why`. The PER-WRITER adjudication is
not duplicated here: it lives in tools/data/writer_dispositions.json with a
reason class per function, gated by tools/gen_writer_attribution.py --check.

BUILDING.why: Matches name_taxonomy; reader mass is overwhelming (12 our_readers + 57 overflow) and dominated by Strategic sim/economy building-management + Strategic AI targeting code. || SIM1-H (2026-09-10): Building became a LIBMH-WRITTEN region this batch -- llm_strat_bldg_init_defaults, the boot-time defaults seeder, is the sim domain's only writer of it and batch H translated it. SB-SOLE's boundary then demands one of two outcomes, and this region takes the second: the two remaining original writers are recorded here with a reason rather than driven to zero. Both are CONFIG-TABLE work at boot, before any tick, and both are per-writer adjudicated in writer_dispositions.json: cfg_final_building_Construct fills the rows from disk, and cfg_CalcBuildingsTechLevel derives upgrade_lvl by walking the upgrade_index chain. Neither touches a field our seeder writes (state_transition_ids, the door/park/dock/pad offsets, pip_slot_count, the sprite anchors), so the two are disjoint by field as well as ordered in time.
BUILDING.kept_writers_why: CONFIG-TABLE LOAD AND DERIVE, boot-only, both before any tick and both disjoint BY FIELD from libmh's only writer. cfg_final_building_Construct fills the Building[] rows from disk (cfg_ConstructBuildings <- ConstructObjects <- cfg_Init); cfg_CalcBuildingsTechLevel then walks each type's upgrade_index successor chain and increments upgrade_lvl, one caller, cfg_Init @0x004a925d. libmh's writer is llm_strat_bldg_init_defaults (SIM1-H), which seeds state_transition_ids, the door/park/dock/shuttle-pad offsets, pip_slot_count and the sprite anchors -- no field either config writer touches. Driving the count to zero would mean translating the .cfg parser, which is LIB-BOOT's territory and not a sim question, so this region takes SB-SOLE's second legal outcome: keep the writers, name them, and say why. Both also carry per-writer rows in writer_dispositions.json.

CREATE_GAME_DEAD_SLIDE_RET.why: Create-game dead-slide return site at 0x004bd9d8. A FUNCTION ADDRESS, NOT STATE. It reaches the registry through dll_addr_manifest.json (the DLL needs its entry address to call or hook it) and gen_state_registry --refresh rebuilds the registry out of the address manifests, so a function anchor arrives as a size-0 pseudo-region. Size 0 is the tell: there is no datum here, and the instruction scan therefore reports it UNMEASURED rather than clean. Classified so the ownership gate is not left red by an entry that can never have an accessor. Surfaced 2026-08-31 by the first registry refresh since these anchors were added; they are not new to the binary.

cross_write_host_config.why: This is the one tactical cross-write that is SUPPOSED to survive, so the plane argument above does not apply to it and must not be read onto it. llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic performs a guarded one-way latch at 0x0044d3f3 / 0x0044d404 -- `if (G_PLANET_STATUS[G_PLANET_INDEX] == UNKNOWN) G_PLANET_STATUS[...] = VISITED` -- and SwitchToPlanet (0x0044cf53) reads exactly that to choose regenerate-vs-load on the next visit to the planet. map_SavePlanetToDisk performs the identical latch (0x00447bef / 0x00447bfe), so this is a reused idiom for `this planet now has persisted content`, not a one-off. IT IS NOT COVERED BY THE PLANET ROUND-TRIP AT ALL: the region sits at offset 0x27 inside the 0x657-byte block that game_SaveGame compresses from _G_LLM_GAME_SESSION_MODE (0x00e58344) and llm_game_load reads back, i.e. it persists through the SAVEGAME. IN-PROCESS the write lands on the live bytes (D4, stock base). STANDALONE no original tactical code exists (LIB-REF). RELOCATED it breaks the same way the planes do -- the original writes the stock base while libmh reads the relocated copy -- and here the consequence is worse than for scratch, because the value is a decision input rather than something the next reload overwrites. NOTE THE CORRECTION: SB2's seed classified this writer `init-only` (`...only finalizes/resets planet status at the tactical-to-strategic session boundary`). That is wrong -- it is the RESULT-producing transition, not an initializer -- and this entry supersedes it. RESTATED, NOT CLEARED (2026-09-06, SB-HOSTFREE). The runtime check this entry asked for now exists: tools/test_ui.py --tact-determinism --tact-relocate runs the second arm under `[harness] relocate_state=1` and compares the per-frame tactical hash against an in-place arm (PASS, SIM and FULL IDENTICAL over 400 frames; mutation-proven with --tact-relocate-corrupt, which diverges at frame 1 naming the corrupted region). It does NOT clear this exception, and the reason is measured rather than argued: the relocating bind REFUSES to move this region, because the accessor census names 3 original accessor(s) that still reach it -- SwitchToPlanet, llm_ui_outcome_dlg_open, llm_ui_render_planet_selector_tooltip. `relocatable` is generated from that census (mh_regions.gen.h, is_movable()), so the refusal is mechanical and will lift by itself when the last of those is promoted. Until then `fails_in: ["relocated-bind"]` stands, and it now stands with names.
cross_write_host_config.check: tools/gen_region_accessors.py --check (the per-writer ratchet, as for the planes) plus tools/gen_region_accessors.py --writers "Tactical mode". A relocated bind is refused by tools/gen_state_registry.py --check rules 1-3 while the SAVE manifest still reaches this region by address -- and it does, via the _G_LLM_GAME_SESSION_MODE block -- so this region cannot be marked owned_by_dll without that block gaining a whole-region serializer first.

INPUT_KEYSTATE.serializer_why: The game's live per-scancode keystate array (KEYSTATE[scancode], set-1 codes), written ONLY by llm_input_wndproc_tap's raw WM_KEYDOWN/UP path (down |= extended?10:5, up &= extended?0xfd:0xfe) or re-latched wholesale from the device by llm_input_di_keyboard_poll. Host input state, not sim state: it is derived from the physical keyboard every frame and is neither hashed nor saved (MF_VIEW only, HASH_REGION_COUNT stays 61). The DLL does not own it -- the harness writes it during a JOURNAL REPLAY only, to reproduce a modifier the recording held, because llm_strat_input_update's squad-merge branch reads the SHIFT bytes here rather than the event ring (harness.cpp tji_keystate_apply / tji_keystate_reassert). Registered so the address has a name; measured extent is 0 because no matrix/shadow/save manifest claims a size for it -- the real array is byte[128], typed in Ghidra at EN v396.
INPUT_KEYSTATE.why: Measured, not inferred. Every named byte inside it (_G_LLM_KEY_LCTRL/LSHIFT/RSHIFT/LALT_HELD at base+0x1D/0x2A/0x36/0x38) shows ~40 READS and ZERO WRITES in the reference manager, because the array is only ever touched by computed index -- the classic 'reads as dead' shape. The writer is llm_input_wndproc_tap @0x004d1194, whose raw WM_KEYDOWN/UP arm does `(&_G_LLM_INPUT_KEYSTATE)[lParam>>16 & 0x7f] |= (lParam & 0x1000000) ? 10 : 5` and the matching &0xfd/&0xfe on key-up; if a DirectInput keyboard device is present it instead delegates to llm_input_di_keyboard_poll, which re-latches the array from the device. Both writers are the game's input layer, so ownership is the game's. Not owned_by_dll: nothing in the migration reimplements either writer, and the harness's replay-time write is a test instrument reproducing recorded input, not a claim on the state.

LLM_UI_MENU_SCREEN_SLIDE_TRANSITION.why: Menu screen slide-transition driver at 0x004bc30e. A FUNCTION ADDRESS, NOT STATE. It reaches the registry through dll_addr_manifest.json (the DLL needs its entry address to call or hook it) and gen_state_registry --refresh rebuilds the registry out of the address manifests, so a function anchor arrives as a size-0 pseudo-region. Size 0 is the tell: there is no datum here, and the instruction scan therefore reports it UNMEASURED rather than clean. Classified so the ownership gate is not left red by an entry that can never have an accessor. Surfaced 2026-08-31 by the first registry refresh since these anchors were added; they are not new to the binary.

MAP_REGION_GRID.cross_write_accepted: phantom-ref: __Nan_Inf DOES NOT WRITE THIS REGION -- corrected 2026-08-28, and `naming-gap` was the wrong diagnosis rather than an imprecise one: it asserted a subsystem-attribution problem where there is no write at all. __Nan_Inf is the Watcom CRT float-formatting helper that emits "inf"/"nan" into the CALLER'S char* (0x00507388 = 69 6E 66 00; 0x0050738c = 6E 61 6E 00). At 0x004f434b `MOV dword ptr [EAX],EDX` the destination is a caller stack buffer, but Ghidra's constant propagation resolved EDX's LOADED VALUE and minted ANALYSIS DATA refs on operand 1 -- one of them to 0x006e616e ("nan"), which lands inside this region's 0x688ac4..0x708ac4 span. gen_state_matrix.py's pass B then took operand 0's WRITE ref-type for that target, because locate_operand cannot find a propagated value in any operand and the single-memory-operand fallback picks [EAX]. It is also NOT caller-less -- _FtoS (0x004f36a3) and __cvt (0x004f438a) call it; it looks orphaned only because call_graph_no_crt.json strips CRT edges. The full disposition lives in tools/data/writer_dispositions.json (class `phantom-ref`); the extractor fix is tracked in tasks/tooling.md and docs/dead-ends.md.

MESSAGE_QUEUE.why: RE-ATTRIBUTED 2026-08-28 from Strategic sim/economy to UI/menus (user's call). The on-screen message ring is PRESENTATION state; the sim posts into it, which is a producer relationship, not ownership. THE OLD REASON WAS A NAME ARGUMENT COMPUTED WITH A BROKEN CLASSIFIER: until commit 0ec6f630 tools/_subsys.py still tested the `::` namespace forms the 2026-08-05 flattening deleted, so game_ui_AddTextToPrintQueue -- the function that actually shifts the ring -- classified as [Other named] and was discounted as an `unclassified accessor` rather than counted as the UI writer it is. This is the RING ITSELF -- the 30-slot on-screen message buffer game_ui_AddTextToPrintQueue shifts (sim_effect_classes.json's verified entry for it says so, @0x00496528), paired with MESSAGE_TIME above. 7,200 B / 30 slots = 240 B per slot, consistent with a wide-char line. IT IS UNMEASURED, so this rests on identity rather than on accessor evidence, and that is stated rather than glossed: the instruction scan never attributed a touch, so the ring is reached through a computed pointer the sweep does not resolve. The previous reason was a SAVE-FORMAT ADJACENCY argument (same 18-block group as INVASION_ALERT_TIME / ADVISOR_NEXT_TIME) -- being serialized with session state says the bytes persist, not who owns them; UI state is saved too.

NETSETUP_IP_CANCEL_INTRO_WAIT_RET.why: Net-setup IP-entry cancel return site at 0x004bd856. A FUNCTION ADDRESS, NOT STATE. It reaches the registry through dll_addr_manifest.json (the DLL needs its entry address to call or hook it) and gen_state_registry --refresh rebuilds the registry out of the address manifests, so a function anchor arrives as a size-0 pseudo-region. Size 0 is the tell: there is no datum here, and the instruction scan therefore reports it UNMEASURED rather than clean. Classified so the ownership gate is not left red by an entry that can never have an accessor. Surfaced 2026-08-31 by the first registry refresh since these anchors were added; they are not new to the binary.

THE RESTORE IS I/O-CONDITIONAL, and this exception is scoped to the case where it succeeds. Measured at instruction level 2026-08-24: the entry gate DISCARDS map_SavePlanetToDisk's return -- 0x0044d38f CALL, then 0x0044d394 MOV GAME_MODE,6 with no TEST between them -- and on the exit a failed map_LoadPlanetFromDisk (0x0044d41d TEST/JNZ) only skips the finalizers: GAME_MODE is already 2 (written at 0x0044d3e4, BEFORE the reload), the planet is already latched VISITED (0x0044d404), the return is discarded by both llm_tact_frame call sites (0x00429c87 and 0x00429df3, each CALL then JMP to the epilogue), and the game continues onto a planet still holding tactical's 128x128 wipe. That is a defect of the ORIGINAL game, not something the migration introduces, and it is recorded as a finding rather than hidden inside this reason. STANDALONE the exception is not needed rather than satisfied: LIB-REF links only libmh and its build-time check confirms it pulls in none of the mh.exe injection layer, so none of these functions exists in that image. RELOCATED is where it BREAKS by construction, and that is the case this entry exists to name: if a host binds a relocated copy of this region while the original tactical code still writes the stock base (SB-HOSTFREE's arrangement), the mission reads stale planes and the reload restores the abandoned copy. No runtime check exercises a tactical excursion under a relocated bind today -- SB-HOSTFREE must either exclude tactical mode from its replay or add one. RE-ATTRIBUTED 2026-08-24 (TACT0): this region's declared owner moved from Strategic sim/economy to Map/geometry -- one map-owned substrate with two mutually-exclusive mode tenants. The adjudication below is unchanged in substance; the write is still a cross-write, still excursion-scoped, and still holds only in the in-process configuration. RESTATED, NOT CLEARED (2026-09-06, SB-HOSTFREE). The runtime check this entry asked for now exists: tools/test_ui.py --tact-determinism --tact-relocate runs the second arm under `[harness] relocate_state=1` and compares the per-frame tactical hash against an in-place arm (PASS, SIM and FULL IDENTICAL over 400 frames; mutation-proven with --tact-relocate-corrupt, which diverges at frame 1 naming the corrupted region). It does NOT clear this exception, and the reason is measured rather than argued: the relocating bind REFUSES to move this region, because the accessor census names 19 original accessor(s) that still reach it -- llm_map_load_objects, llm_map_load_objects_loose, llm_map_passable_mark_annulus_clear, llm_map_passable_mark_annulus_set, llm_tact_move_find_approach_tile, llm_map_build_regions and 13 more. `relocatable` is generated from that census (mh_regions.gen.h, is_movable()), so the refusal is mechanical and will lift by itself when the last of those is promoted. Until then `fails_in: ["relocated-bind"]` stands, and it now stands with names.

LIB-REF's build-time check is the standalone gate. UNMEASURED IS NOT CLEAN -- per gen_region_accessors' own rule a size-0 region contains no address and is structurally invisible to every attribution-derived check. Owner declared from the menu-slide family it belongs to; giving it a real extent is RI-STATE's job, not an ownership question.

SND_AMBIENT_BY_PLANET.cross_write_accepted: producer-consumer across the mode boundary: llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic [Tactical mode] calls llm_snd_ambient_reseed_planet_event_times (0x0045e277) on the way out of a mission, which restamps [G_PLANET_INDEX].events[0..19].next_time so the strategic ambient schedule does not fire a backlog on re-entry. It reaches the table through the Sound module's own reseed entry point rather than writing fields itself.
SND_AMBIENT_BY_PLANET.why: Every function that names the base address is an ambient-sound routine -- llm_snd_ambient_tick, llm_snd_ambient_add, llm_snd_ambient_planet_clone and llm_snd_ambient_init_tables (whole-image instruction sweep for the LE dword, 10 sites) -- and the type is llm_snd_ambient_planet_list[32], one ambient-event list per planet. Registered 2026-08-27 to close finding 2026-08-24-1830-2: it was a write destination in no registry region at all, so gen_region_accessors, the cross-write adjudication and the ST3 interlock were all blind to it.
SND_AMBIENT_BY_PLANET.kept_writers_why: SB-SOLE: 4 original writer(s) kept. Reason class(es): permanent-wall (render/UI/platform, a declared non-goal of the revised M6 exit). Per-writer reasons: tools/data/writer_dispositions.json.

SND_CHANNEL_NEXT_RETRIGGER_TIME.why: The per-channel retrigger clock of the SOUND layer: llm_snd_stop_all_channels zeroes all six elements with an indexed channel*8 loop, which is what proves the double[6] shape at all. Measured writers Tactical mode 5 / Sound 2, but the tactical writes are all llm_tact_ambient_sound_tick stamping ITS OWN channel-0 slot -- a client of the region, not its owner.

SND_ENABLED.why: The sound-enable gate. Registered because llm_game_reload_snapshot_resync_clocks (lib_trans batch D) saves/zeroes/restores it around the alert-emitter re-basing calls -- the region belongs to the sound subsystem (a wall); the lib_trans row only needs the write to be routable.
SND_ENABLED.cross_write_accepted: producer-consumer: the three Game/boot writers (init_first_run_defaults, debug console, and reload_snapshot_resync_clocks's save/zero/restore around the alert re-basing calls) toggle the gate the Sound subsystem consumes on every play call. A master-enable switch is written by whoever owns the moment (boot, debug, reload), read by Sound -- the cross-write is the design, not drift.

SQUAD_BB_SCAN_PLAYER.why: Blackboard scalar: the player whose squad is assaulting. Declared 2026-08-23 (TACT-PREP); see docs/tactical-probe.md.
SQUAD_BB_SCAN_PLAYER.cross_write_accepted:
boundary-by-design: not a mis-attribution -- the same reason already accepted for SQUAD_STATUS_COUNT, and for the same writer. llm_strat_bldg_gather_nearby_squad_status is the strategic-side ENTRY to a tactical mission: it fills the blackboard and returns the slot count, and a zero return is what makes the entry gate refuse. The record exists only to carry a tactical result across the mode transition, so attributing it to the sim would put a region no sim tick ever touches inside the sim's writer closure (docs/tactical-probe.md Sect. 5).
SURFACED 2026-08-24 by the readers readiness drain, and worth recording WHY it was invisible until then: all five blackboard scalars sat in the registry at size 0. A zero-length span contains no address, so tmp/state_matrix.json attributed no access to them from ANY function and the cross-write adjudication had nothing to fire on -- the R6 unmeasurable-region trap, reading green because it could not read at all. Typing the four Ghidra symbols as `int` gave them a measurable extent, and the writes appeared. SQUAD_BB_TARGET_ENERGY_PCT is the control: it was typed in the same pass and is listed here for the same reason.

SQUAD_STATUS.cross_write_accepted: boundary-by-design: not a mis-attribution -- llm_strat_bldg_gather_nearby_squad_status [Strategic sim/economy] is the strategic-side ENTRY to a tactical mission, filling the blackboard before the mode switch, and llm_strat_squad_assault_resolve [Strategic sim/economy] is the strategic-side EXIT reading it back after the mode switch. Both are the mode boundary itself, not a sim writer of tactical state; the ongoing per-frame writer during the mission is llm_tact_squad_sync_hp [Tactical mode], matching the declared owner (same reasoning as SQUAD_STATUS_COUNT's existing cross_write_accepted).
SQUAD_STATUS.why: The 64-slot stride-0x10 squad record array (llm_squad_status_slot: unit_proto_id, energy_pct, unit_slot_index, is_commando -- typed 2026-08-26, TACT1A batch A) that carries a tactical mission across the mode transition: filled by llm_strat_bldg_gather_nearby_squad_status at entry, refreshed by llm_tact_squad_sync_hp ONCE at the mission-exit-confirm moment (not every frame -- both of llm_tact_frame's call sites sit immediately before llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic), consumed by llm_strat_squad_assault_resolve at exit. Owned by tactical because it exists ONLY to carry a tactical result; the two strat-named accessors are the boundary, not the owner. Deliberately absent from the save block table, which is exactly why it survives the planet reload that restores the three shared map planes. Declared 2026-08-23 (TACT-PREP); see docs/tactical-probe.md. Region was previously named SQUAD_BLACKBOARD with size 0 (untyped -- the ref-manager-blindness trap, docs/dead-ends.md G44): renamed to match its own plates' _G_LLM_SQUAD_STATUS and typed to its real 1024-byte extent 2026-08-26.

SQUAD_STATUS_COUNT.why: How many SQUAD_BLACKBOARD slots are valid. gather() returns it and a zero return is what makes the tactical entry gate refuse. Declared 2026-08-23 (TACT-PREP); see docs/tactical-probe.md.
SQUAD_STATUS_COUNT.cross_write_accepted: boundary-by-design: not a mis-attribution -- llm_strat_bldg_gather_nearby_squad_status is the strategic-side ENTRY to a tactical mission -- it fills the blackboard and returns this count, and a zero return is what makes the entry gate refuse. The region exists only to carry a tactical result across the mode transition and is refreshed by llm_tact_squad_sync_hp once, at the mission-exit-confirm moment (corrected 2026-08-26 from 'every tactical frame' -- find-cross-references' call-site context shows both of llm_tact_frame's call sites sit immediately before llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic), so attributing it to the sim would put a region no sim tick ever touches inside the sim's writer closure. The cross-write IS the mode boundary (docs/tactical-probe.md Sect. 5).

STONES.why: cfg::final::data::Stones -- a post-cfg prototype table of the strategic resource-rock objects, built by cfg_ConstructStones. The state matrix has no region entry for this address at all, so the census reports no accessor either way; the two references Ghidra does record are the dead llm_cfg_save/load_final_snapshot pair. Attributed to the strategic sim by the table's role, matching its Building/Unit/Planets siblings, not by a measured accessor -- and that gap is exactly why LIB-BOOT carries it on the retail-snapshot evidence.

NOT a session-entry seed -- a PROCESS-LIFETIME LATCH: nothing zero-inits the region per session (the only 0-writer is the tutorial driver), so after one New Game every later session in the process inherits 1, and a process that never presses New Game runs with the .bss 0 and no strategic AI at all. G174 MEMBER, LOUD-FAILURE VARIANT: MF_VIEW means no hash/shadow/save gate can see a regression here, and the MP determinism path never presses New Game (0 on both peers) -- but the failure mode is loud, not silent: llm_strat_sim_step's head gate turns the whole AI pipeline on/off, so a wrong value diverges any AI-bearing arm at ~step 1. With UI/menus as the owner the UI writers agree, and the cross-writers are llm_net_chat_input_process [Netcode], feeding a chat line, and llm_strat_input_update [Strategic sim/economy], the input wall. Unchanged in substance from the pre-2026-08-28 reason; only the direction is corrected.
STRAT_FLOATING_MSG_COLOR.serializer_why: Sole reader llm_strat_draw_floating_messages actually renders using this color, matching name_taxonomy; it is a producer/consumer scratch value written by whichever subsystem queues a floating message right before the strat renderer consumes it.
STRAT_FLOATING_MSG_COLOR.why: RE-ATTRIBUTED 2026-08-28 from Strategic sim/economy to UI/menus (user's call). The on-screen message ring is PRESENTATION state; the sim posts into it, which is a producer relationship, not ownership. THE OLD REASON WAS A NAME ARGUMENT COMPUTED WITH A BROKEN CLASSIFIER: until commit 0ec6f630 tools/_subsys.py still tested the `::` namespace forms the 2026-08-05 flattening deleted, so game_ui_AddTextToPrintQueue -- the function that actually shifts the ring -- classified as [Other named] and was discounted as an `unclassified accessor` rather than counted as the UI writer it is. Five writers, and four are presentation outright: llm_ui_print_floating_msg_cyan / _red and game_ui_AddTextToPrintQueue [UI/menus] plus llm_net_chat_input_process [Netcode] setting the colour for a chat line. The fifth, llm_strat_input_update, is the input wall. The SOLE READER llm_strat_draw_floating_messages renders with it. The previous reason said 'matching name_taxonomy' in as many words -- i.e. it was the prefix, and the prefix is what is wrong here.

STRAT_FLOATING_MSG_QUEUE_ACTIVE.cross_write_accepted: producer-consumer: every cross-writer POSTS into the ring rather than owning it -- llm_strat_advisor_tick (advisor notifications), llm_strat_bldg_try_begin_placement (the build-placement refusal message), llm_strat_input_update (the input wall), llm_net_chat_input_process and our own llm_net_lockstep_dispatch (chat / lockstep event text), and llm_cfg_text_ptrs_reset clearing it when the text table is rebuilt. Our llm_strat_sim_tick likewise posts rather than owns; see `why` for why the resulting lint_arch R3 edges are the lint working rather than a regression.
STRAT_FLOATING_MSG_QUEUE_ACTIVE.serializer_why: Majority of writers (llm_strat_advisor_tick, llm_strat_bldg_try_begin_placement, llm_strat_input_update) plus our_writer llm_strat_sim_tick are Strategic sim/economy, matching name_taxonomy_says; the advisor floating-message system is tick-driven strategic-mode UI feedback.
STRAT_FLOATING_MSG_QUEUE_ACTIVE.why: RE-ATTRIBUTED 2026-08-28 from Strategic sim/economy to UI/menus (user's call). The on-screen message ring is PRESENTATION state; the sim posts into it, which is a producer relationship, not ownership. THE OLD REASON WAS A NAME ARGUMENT COMPUTED WITH A BROKEN CLASSIFIER: until commit 0ec6f630 tools/_subsys.py still tested the `::` namespace forms the 2026-08-05 flattening deleted, so game_ui_AddTextToPrintQueue -- the function that actually shifts the ring -- classified as [Other named] and was discounted as an `unclassified accessor` rather than counted as the UI writer it is. THE OLD REASON WAS A MAJORITY-OF-WRITERS ARGUMENT AND THE MAJORITY DOES NOT HOLD ON BEHAVIOUR. It named llm_strat_advisor_tick, llm_strat_bldg_try_begin_placement and llm_strat_input_update as the sim majority: input_update is the input wall, bldg_try_begin_placement is the UI build-placement click path, and only advisor_tick is sim -- and what advisor_tick does here is POST A MESSAGE, which is the producer relationship, not ownership. NOTE WHAT THIS COSTS AND WHY IT IS ACCEPTED: our own llm_strat_sim_tick and llm_net_lockstep_dispatch write this flag, so re-attributing it turns those into lint_arch R3 edges (sim/net WRITE -> ui region). That is the lint working, not a regression -- the original game genuinely has its tick poke presentation state, and the edge was invisible only while the region was mislabelled sim. lint_arch is a burn-down REPORT, not a gate, and its own header says an edge is a lead rather than a finding.

Per-writer reasons: tools/data/writer_dispositions.json.

cross_write_host_config.why: IN-PROCESS this is a shared write, not a wrong one: under D4 (docs/state-boundary.md) the host answers the bind table with the stock .bss base, so the original tactical code writes exactly the bytes libmh reads. The reuse is INCIDENTAL and excursion-scoped -- entry saves the whole planet (map_SavePlanetToDisk 0x00447bb3) before llm_tact_map_reset wipes anything, and llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic re-reads it (map_LoadPlanetFromDisk 0x00448107); tools/data/save_block_table.json shows the two block lists are 44-for-44 symmetric and carry this region at its exact base and full size in both directions, with no in-memory copy-back anywhere. All 22 live writers below are EXCLUSIVELY TACTICAL by the committed closure (tools/data/tact_closure.json): reachable only from llm_tact_mission_start / llm_tact_frame / llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic, which llm_frame_dispatch gates on _G_LLM_GAME_MODE == 6. THE RESTORE IS I/O-CONDITIONAL, and this exception is scoped to the case where it succeeds. Measured at instruction level 2026-08-24: the entry gate DISCARDS map_SavePlanetToDisk's return -- 0x0044d38f CALL, then 0x0044d394 MOV GAME_MODE,6 with no TEST between them -- and on the exit a failed map_LoadPlanetFromDisk (0x0044d41d TEST/JNZ) only skips the finalizers: GAME_MODE is already 2 (written at 0x0044d3e4, BEFORE the reload), the planet is already latched VISITED (0x0044d404), the return is discarded by both llm_tact_frame call sites (0x00429c87 and 0x00429df3, each CALL then JMP to the epilogue), and the game continues onto a planet still holding tactical's 128x128 wipe. That is a defect of the ORIGINAL game, not something the migration introduces, and it is recorded as a finding rather than hidden inside this reason. STANDALONE the exception is not needed rather than satisfied: LIB-REF links only libmh and its build-time check confirms it pulls in none of the mh.exe injection layer, so none of these functions exists in that image. RELOCATED is where it BREAKS by construction, and that is the case this entry exists to name: if a host binds a relocated copy of this region while the original tactical code still writes the stock base (SB-HOSTFREE's arrangement), the mission reads stale planes and the reload restores the abandoned copy. No runtime check exercises a tactical excursion under a relocated bind today -- SB-HOSTFREE must either exclude tactical mode from its replay or add one. RE-ATTRIBUTED 2026-08-24 (TACT0): this region's declared owner moved from Strategic sim/economy to Map/geometry -- one map-owned substrate with two mutually-exclusive mode tenants. The adjudication below is unchanged in substance; the write is still a cross-write, still excursion-scoped, and still holds only in the in-process configuration. RESTATED, NOT CLEARED (2026-09-06, SB-HOSTFREE). The runtime check this entry asked for now exists: tools/test_ui.py --tact-determinism --tact-relocate runs the second arm under `[harness] relocate_state=1` and compares the per-frame tactical hash against an in-place arm (PASS, SIM and FULL IDENTICAL over 400 frames; mutation-proven with --tact-relocate-corrupt, which diverges at frame 1 naming the corrupted region). Written by Game/boot entry points (llm_game_land_players_on_planet, llm_game_start_tutorial, llm_strat_planet_session_begin, llm_strat_session_begin_multi) as they hand a freshly configured world to the sim. cross_write_host_config.why: IN-PROCESS this is a shared write, not a wrong one: under D4 (docs/state-boundary.md) the host answers the bind table with the stock .bss base, so the original tactical code writes exactly the bytes libmh reads. The reuse is INCIDENTAL and excursion-scoped -- entry saves the whole planet (map_SavePlanetToDisk 0x00447bb3) before llm_tact_map_reset wipes anything, and llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic re-reads it (map_LoadPlanetFromDisk 0x00448107); tools/data/save_block_table.json shows the two block lists are 44-for-44 symmetric and carry this region at its exact base and full size in both directions, with no in-memory copy-back anywhere. All 22 live writers below are EXCLUSIVELY TACTICAL by the committed closure (tools/data/tact_closure.json): reachable only from llm_tact_mission_start / llm_tact_frame / llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic, which llm_frame_dispatch gates on _G_LLM_GAME_MODE == 6. THE RESTORE IS I/O-CONDITIONAL, and this exception is scoped to the case where it succeeds. Measured at instruction level 2026-08-24: the entry gate DISCARDS map_SavePlanetToDisk's return -- 0x0044d38f CALL, then 0x0044d394 MOV GAME_MODE,6 with no TEST between them -- and on the exit a failed map_LoadPlanetFromDisk (0x0044d41d TEST/JNZ) only skips the finalizers: GAME_MODE is already 2 (written at 0x0044d3e4, BEFORE the reload), the planet is already latched VISITED (0x0044d404), the return is discarded by both llm_tact_frame call sites (0x00429c87 and 0x00429df3, each CALL then JMP to the epilogue), and the game continues onto a planet still holding tactical's 128x128 wipe. That is a defect of the ORIGINAL game, not something the migration introduces, and it is recorded as a finding rather than hidden inside this reason. STANDALONE the exception is not needed rather than satisfied: LIB-REF links only libmh and its build-time check confirms it pulls in none of the mh.exe injection layer, so none of these functions exists in that image. RELOCATED is where it BREAKS by construction, and that is the case this entry exists to name: if a host binds a relocated copy of this region while the original tactical code still writes the stock base (SB-HOSTFREE's arrangement), the mission reads stale planes and the reload restores the abandoned copy. No runtime check exercises a tactical excursion under a relocated bind today -- SB-HOSTFREE must either exclude tactical mode from its replay or add one. RE-ATTRIBUTED 2026-08-24 (TACT0): this region's declared owner moved from Strategic sim/economy to Map/geometry -- one map-owned substrate with two mutually-exclusive mode tenants. The adjudication below is unchanged in substance; the write is still a cross-write, still excursion-scoped, and still holds only in the in-process configuration. RESTATED, NOT CLEARED (2026-09-06, SB-HOSTFREE). The runtime check this entry asked for now exists: tools/test_ui.py --tact-determinism --tact-relocate runs the second arm under `[harness] relocate_state=1` and compares the per-frame tactical hash against an in-place arm (PASS, SIM and FULL IDENTICAL over 400 frames; mutation-proven with --tact-relocate-corrupt, which diverges at frame 1 naming the corrupted region). It does NOT clear this exception, and the reason is measured rather than argued: the relocating bind REFUSES to move this region, because the accessor census names 44 original accessor(s) that still reach it -- llm_map_load_main_plane, llm_map_load_main_plane_loose, llm_map_load_objects, llm_map_load_objects_loose, llm_map_tile_find_enemy_of_type, llm_map_tile_find_own_of_type and 38 more. `relocatable` is generated from that census (mh_regions.gen.h, is_movable()), so the refusal is mechanical and will lift by itself when the last of those is promoted. Until then `fails_in: ["relocated-bind"]` stands, and it now stands with names.

TUTORIAL_RESET_SLOT_0050A678.why: SIM-RESID-READY (2026-08-31): llm_game_start_tutorial WRITES it. THE OWNER IS DECLARED FROM THE WRITERS, NOT FROM A MEANING, because the meaning is genuinely unresolved and this item refused to invent one -- the name is a PROVENANCE name keeping the address, the way CRT_<addr> does. All four referrers are links in one Watcom chained store (`BUILD_TYPE_FILTER = X678 = PENDING_BUILD_PLACEMENT_ID = RMB_LIMIT_FLAG = 0`) emitted twice, by llm_game_start_tutorial and llm_ui_menu_close_to_hud; both sites only ever store 0 and nothing consumes the value. Game/boot/misc matches its three chain-siblings, all of which are declared there. THE LIVE ALTERNATIVE: it may be _G_LLM_STRAT_UI_PANEL_FALLBACK_TABLE[4] (that table is int[4] at 0x0050a668, index 4 lands exactly here, and both consumers -- game_SetEvent 0x004140aa and llm_tutorial_step_driver 0x004bae3f -- walk it UNBOUNDED to the first zero, so a NUL-terminated list structurally needs a zero at [4]; that access path leaves no xref, dead-ends.md SectA). If that is confirmed the region should be MERGED INTO that table and this declaration deleted -- the experiment is in the manifest note. Binding is correct under both readings, because a 0 store to a fixed address is the same write either way and Law 1 freezes the layout.
TUTORIAL_RESET_SLOT_0050A678.cross_write_accepted: CLASS E -- THE MENU PATH CLEARS TUTORIAL STATE ON THE WAY OUT. llm_ui_menu_close_to_hud (UI/menus) emits the identical zero-chain that llm_game_start_tutorial does, over the same four fields; its three siblings are declared class E for exactly this. Deferred menu-GFX sprite index for the race-select overlay: the Human/Alien buttons' shared draw_cb (0x004b935c) STORES an index here rather than drawing, and widget 0x0065087b flushes it -- blits MENU_GFX_HANDLES[idx] (table 0x0065419f, SHL 2) at its own x/y and clears it. 0 = nothing pending. NAMED ON DIRECT EVIDENCE, not adjacency: the four indices the code computes (0x0f/0x10/0x11/0x12) are exactly RACEHH/RACEHS/RACEAH/RACEAS in the resource-name table at 0x00604288, H=hovered S=selected, and both race widgets carry action_cb llm_menu_race_select_cb. SIX of its seven referrers sit in code Ghidra never made into a function (block entries 0x004b845e and 0x004b935c, both clean Watcom prologues, neither a jump-table case) -- read as bytes, deliberately NOT create-function'd.

No sim or boot code ever reads it; the only reader is the UI draw callback that flushes it. So no value crosses the boundary, and the owner remains the menu code that produces and consumes it.
UI_RACE_SEL_PENDING_GFX_IDX.kept_writers_why: MARK REMOVED, WRITER KEPT (ST3 rule 10, 2026-09-12) -- and this region's own `why` already NAMED both writers before the census could see them: 0x004b845e and 0x004b935c were described there as block entries Ghidra had not made into functions. Menu GFX end to end: OWN_ISLAND, MF_VIEW only, and libmh's single writer (llm_game_start_tutorial) also writes only zero. Consequence: no relocation or standalone host while the menu owns this staging slot. SURFACED BY THE EN v405 CENSUS REFRESH (2026-09-12), not by a new write: the committed region_accessors.json was built from a 10,861-cell matrix and the fresh one has 10,982, so these writers were latent in the census, not absent from the binary -- tmp/state_matrix_v404 already holds the identical cells and the MOVS-resolved site count is 232 in BOTH matrices, so none of this is a MOVS heuristic artefact.
